name: Tor Exit Nodes Scraping Pricing API
description: A competitor (or someone running for one) hammers /api/v3/pricing through ~40 Tor exit nodes to dodge IP-based rate limits. Each individual IP looks like a normal user, but the aggregate pulls a full price book every two hours. The pricing service stays up but the Postgres read replica falls behind on lag.
reasoning: Edge nginx → pricing-api (Go) → primary + read replica. Most reads go to the replica; the scraping pattern hits cold parts of the catalog so the replica's working set churns and replication lag grows.

narrative.text: Normal day-shift traffic; cache hit ratio on /pricing 92%.
Anomaly: requests from ~40 ASNs all matching known Tor exit list, low rate per IP, overlapping crawl pattern.
Working set on pricing-pg-ro churns; cache hit drops to 60%.
Replication lag grows to 12s as replica spends cycles on cold-page reads.
Pattern repeats — crawler restarts every ~7000 requests. Bot-detector flags it for review.
Risk team blocks Tor exits at the WAF for /api/v3/* endpoints.
Replica catches up; cache hit recovers to 88%.
Steady state; long-term plan: per-account auth on bulk pricing endpoints.
